questions.question: Pooja gets a discount of 17% on a dryer whose marked price is ₹2,000. Since she pays by credit card, she gets an additional 10% discount. How much does she pay (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **successive discounts** are 17% and 10% on the **Marked Price**.

Final Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)%

Final Selling Price = 2000 × 83% × 90%

Final Selling Price = 2000 × 0.83 × 0.9 = 1494

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1494.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹2,000

**First Discount** = 17%

**Additional Discount** (Credit Card) = 10%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91aff31940b50ea283d650c082e01c8d9aad4022aa8906435f93dd2d84c3b9c1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 17% **discount** = 2000 − (17/100 × 2000)

⇒ Price after 17% **discount** = 2000 − 340 = ₹1,660

⇒ Additional 10% **discount** on ₹1,660 = 10/100 × 1660 = ₹166

⇒ Final amount paid by **Pooja** = 1660 − 166 = ₹1,494

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1494.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Discount and Selling Price

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) − Discount. Also, Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

The relation between CP and MP is given by MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

questions.question: At present, a father is 30 years older than his son. In 12 years, the father will be three times as old as his son. What is the present age of the son?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **age difference** between two people always remains **constant** (30 years).

In 12 years, the ratio of **Father** : **Son** = 3 : 1.

Difference in ratio parts = 3 − 1 = 2 units ⇒ 30 years.

1 unit = 15 years (This is the **son's age** after 12 years).

Present age of son = 15 − 12 = 3 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Current age difference = 30 years. Multiplier after 12 years = 3.

**Formula Used:** Age after **n** years = Present age + **n**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24e54436354195a08be2cd5e0c73a7d02ad2a903baaa1c7bd108debca0d2fd46.png] 

⇒ Let the **Present age** of the **son** be **S**.

⇒ Then, **Father's present age** = S + 30.

⇒ After 12 years, **Father's age** = (S + 30) + 12 = S + 42.

⇒ After 12 years, **Son's age** = S + 12.

⇒ According to the question: S + 42 = 3 × (S + 12)

⇒ S + 42 = 3S + 36

⇒ 42 − 36 = 3S − S

⇒ 6 = 2S

⇒ S = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical **difference** between the ages of two individuals **never changes**, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Method in Ages

When ages are given in ratios at different times, adjust the **ratio difference** to match the **actual age difference** to find values quickly.

Average Age Calculation

If the **average age** of **n** people is **A**, then after **k** years, their new average age will be **A + k**.

questions.question: If 9 workers can build a wall in 12 days, how many days will 6 workers take to build the same wall, assuming they work at the same rate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work is **constant**, so use the formula: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂.

9 **workers** × 12 **days** = 6 **workers** × D₂

108 = 6 × D₂

D₂ = 108 ÷ 6 = 18 **days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of workers (M₁) = 9

Initial time taken (D₁) = 12 days

New number of workers (M₂) = 6

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Workers × Number of Days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d58432de6a8d96fa24056f90bf83f470edfbf4eb454275024b7c73037e829cb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work done by 9 workers in 12 days = 9 × 12 = 108 man-days

⇒ Since the wall is the same, 6 workers must complete the same 108 man-days of work.

⇒ Days taken by 6 workers = Total Work ÷ M₂

⇒ Days = 108 ÷ 6

⇒ Days = 18 days

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation in Work

When the **rate of work** is constant, the number of workers is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. If workers decrease, time increases proportionally.

The Chain Rule (M-D-H Formula)

For different work quantities or hours per day: (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂, where H is **hours** and W is **units of work**.

Efficiency Concept

**Efficiency** × **Time** = **Total Work**. Efficiency is the work done per unit of time (e.g., 1 day or 1 hour).

questions.question:
Find the value of m which satisfies

 ((19)/(10))⁷ times ((10)/(19))⁶ times ((19)/(10))¹⁰ = ((10)/(19))⁶m ⁺ ¹⁸
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Convert all terms to the **same base** (19/10) to compare the **exponents** directly. LHS total power = 7 + (−6) + 10 = 11. RHS power = −(6m + 18) = −6m − 18. Equating powers: 11 = −6m − 18 ⇒ 6m = −29. **∴ The correct answer is −29/6.**

questions.question: If x is the mean proportional between (a+b) and (a-b), then find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **mean proportional** **x** between two numbers **m** and **n** is calculated using **x = √(m × n)**.

Substitute **m = (a + b)** and **n = (a − b)**.

**x = √((a + b) × (a − b))**

Using the identity **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²**, we get **x = √(a² − b²)**.

**∴ The correct answer is √(a² − b²).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The terms are **(a + b)** and **(a − b)**, and their **mean proportional** is **x**.

**Formula Used:** If three quantities **A**, **B**, and **C** are in **continued proportion**, then **A : B = B : C**, which means **B² = A × C**. Here, **B** is the mean proportional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/278339999b504b4591a83f042f49154ea29e621c3426e85a2997c2a73be66c0b.png] 

⇒ **(a + b) / x = x / (a − b)**

⇒ **x² = (a + b) × (a − b)**

⇒ We know that **(x + y)(x − y) = x² − y²**

⇒ **x² = a² − b²**

⇒ **x = √(a² − b²)**

**∴ The correct answer is √(a² − b²).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

For two numbers **a** and **b**, the **third proportional** **c** is calculated as **c = b² / a**, where **a : b = b : c**.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c**, the **fourth proportional** **d** is calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**, where **a : b = c : d**.

Continued Proportion

Quantities **a**, **b**, **c**, **d** are in **continued proportion** if **a/b = b/c = c/d**.

questions.question: The difference between a discount of 35% and two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on a certain marked price is ₹70. Find the marked price (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **successive discount** of 20% and 15% = 20 + 15 − (20 × 15)/100 = 32%.

Difference between 35% and 32% = 3%.

Given, 3% of **Marked Price** = ₹70.

Total MP (100%) = (70 ÷ 3) × 100 = 7000 ÷ 3 ≈ ₹2,333.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,333.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Single discount percentage = 35%

Two successive discount percentages = 20% and 15%

Difference between the two discount amounts = ₹70

**Formula Used:**

Equivalent single discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (ab/100)]%

Discount Amount = (Discount% / 100) × **Marked Price**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/969df42da771e519733430550ce287ef46023a8280b3e75583e57aa414d240ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** be M.

⇒ Equivalent of successive discounts = 20 + 15 − (20 × 15)/100 = 35 − 3 = 32%

⇒ First discount amount = 0.35M

⇒ Second discount amount = 0.32M

⇒ Difference = 0.35M − 0.32M = 0.03M

⇒ 0.03M = 70

⇒ M = 70 / 0.03 = 7000 / 3

⇒ M = 2333.333...

⇒ Rounded to nearest integer, M = 2,333.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,333.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, first find equivalent of a and b as x%, then find equivalent of x and c. Effective = x + c − (xc/100).

Relationship between MP and CP

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%). This is used when both profit and discount percentages are given.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) for multiple discounts.

questions.question: The enrolment of students in an institution increased by 10% in April compared to the number of students in March and then decreased by 5%, resulting in 1045 students in June. Find the number of students in March.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = 10 − 5 − (10 × 5 ÷ 100) = 4.5% increase.

Final enrolment in June = 100% + 4.5% = 104.5%.

Given, 104.5% = 1045 students.

March enrolment (100%) = (1045 ÷ 104.5) × 100 = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Enrolment in **June** = 1045

**Increase** in April = 10%

**Decrease** in May/June = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b31b2cc5f9f1d32627aa15b024d8f485459ec7cce5d0b7197fa53919c506d5b.png] 

Let the number of students in **March** be x.

⇒ Students in **April** = x + (10 ÷ 100) × x = 1.1x

⇒ Students in **June** = 1.1x − (5 ÷ 100) × 1.1x

⇒ 1045 = 1.1x × 0.95

⇒ 1045 = 1.045x

⇒ x = 1045 ÷ 1.045

⇒ x = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Multiplying Factor Method

An increase of r% is equivalent to multiplying by (1 + r/100), and a decrease of r% is equivalent to multiplying by (1 − r/100).

Base Value Property

The original value (March in this case) is always considered the 100% base for initial calculations.

questions.question: What is the arithmetic mean of the dataset {12, 25, 37, 48, 56, 61, 73, 85, 92, 104}?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **Assumed Mean** (A) = 60.

Deviations from 60: −48, −35, −23, −12, −4, +1, +13, +25, +32, +44.

Sum of deviations (Σd) = −7.

Average deviation = Σd ÷ n = −7 ÷ 10 = −0.7.

Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + Average Deviation = 60 − 0.7 = 59.3.

**∴ The correct answer is 59.3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dataset = {12, 25, 37, 48, 56, 61, 73, 85, 92, 104}

**Formula Used:**

Arithmetic Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62fe7a19c1b3062f7febf67511e773efedef340c26157148e42082cc6535bf15.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 12 + 25 + 37 + 48 + 56 + 61 + 73 + 85 + 92 + 104

⇒ Sum = 593

⇒ Total count (n) = 10

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 593 ÷ 10

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 59.3

**∴ The correct answer is 59.3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median

The middle value of a sorted dataset. For even **n**, it is the average of the two middle terms: (56 + 61) ÷ 2 = 58.5.

Range

The difference between the maximum and minimum values: 104 − 12 = 92.

Relation between Mean, Median, and Mode

Empirical formula: **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**.

questions.question: The expenditures of R are 65% of his salary. If his salary increased by 10% and his savings are ₹3,150 more than previous savings, his expenditures are now 60% of his salary. His present salary is ₹______.
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of **Initial Salary** to **New Salary** = 100 : 110 **Initial Savings** = 35% of 100 = 35 units **New Savings** = 40% of 110 = 44 units (Since new Expenditure is 60%) Difference in Savings = 44 − 35 = 9 units → ₹3,150 1 unit = 3150 ÷ 9 = 350 **Present Salary** = 110 × 350 = ₹38,500 **∴ The correct answer is ₹38,500.**

questions.question: The value of ((2.3)³ + (1.5)³ + (1.2)³ - 3 times 2.3 times 1.5 times 1.2)/((2.3)² + (1.5)² + (1.2)² - 2.3 times 1.5 - 1.5 times 1.2 - 1.2 times 2.3) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression is in the standard form of the **algebraic identity**: (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca).

This identity simplifies directly to **(a + b + c)**.

Here, a = 2.3, b = 1.5, and c = 1.2.

Required Value = 2.3 + 1.5 + 1.2 = 5.0.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a = 2.3

b = 1.5

c = 1.2

**Formula Used:**

The **sum of cubes** identity states: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expression = ((2.3)³ + (1.5)³ + (1.2)³ − 3 × 2.3 × 1.5 × 1.2) ÷ ((2.3)² + (1.5)² + (1.2)² − 2.3 × 1.5 − 1.5 × 1.2 − 1.2 × 2.3)

⇒ Let a = 2.3, b = 1.5, c = 1.2

⇒ Expression = (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ Expression = [(a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)] ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ Expression = a + b + c

⇒ Expression = 2.3 + 1.5 + 1.2

⇒ Expression = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Special Case of the Identity

If **a + b + c = 0**, then the identity simplifies to **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc**.

Alternative Form of the Quadratic Part

The term (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) can also be written as **1/2[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]**.

Basic Algebraic Identities

Remember **(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)**, which is often used to find missing components of the cubic identity.

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive integers is 10. What is the smallest integer?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an odd number of **consecutive integers**, the **average** is always the **middle term**.

Middle term (3rd term) = 10.

The sequence is: 8, 9, **10**, 11, 12.

The **smallest integer** is the first term of this sequence.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **consecutive integers** (n) = 5

**Average** of the integers = 10

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4144be46218c36de315ab63c9118190ff7770ee7a16b4c0f753a18895ad2433a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the five **consecutive integers** be x, (x + 1), (x + 2), (x + 3), and (x + 4).

⇒ Sum = x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3) + (x + 4) = 5x + 10

⇒ Average = (5x + 10) ÷ 5 = 10

⇒ x + 2 = 10

⇒ x = 10 − 2

⇒ x = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence in **Arithmetic Progression**, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Sum of Consecutive Integers

The sum of **n consecutive integers** starting from x is given by n × x + [n × (n − 1) ÷ 2].

Middle Term Property

If **n is odd**, the average is exactly the **{(n + 1) ÷ 2}th** term of the consecutive sequence.

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 8, and their LCM is 7072. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of the **ratio parts** = 17 × 13 × 8 = 1768.

Since the ratio parts 17, 13, and 8 are **pairwise co-prime**, their **LCM** is their product multiplied by the **HCF**.

**HCF** = Given **LCM** ÷ Product of **ratio parts**.

**HCF** = 7072 ÷ 1768 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of numbers = 17 : 13 : 8, **LCM** = 7072.

**Formula:** If numbers are in ratio a : b : c and their **HCF** is x, then the numbers are ax, bx, and cx. Their **LCM** is x × LCM(a, b, c).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d7eb165a88ac00d96296ad583cb08c1614c939647f0075b6314718c812cfcf5.png] 

⇒ Let the three numbers be 17x, 13x, and 8x, where **x** is the **HCF**.

⇒ The **LCM** of 17x, 13x, and 8x is calculated by taking the common factor **x** and the **LCM** of (17, 13, 8).

⇒ **LCM** = x × 17 × 13 × 8

⇒ 7072 = 1768 × x

⇒ x = 7072 ÷ 1768

⇒ x = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Property of HCF and LCM

For two numbers a and b: **Product of numbers = HCF × LCM**. This property does not directly apply to three or more numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Numbers that have only 1 as their **common factor** are called **co-prime**. The **LCM** of a set of **pairwise co-prime** numbers is always their product.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

**HCF** = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators) | **LCM** = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

questions.question: A sum of ₹25,000 is invested at 2% per annum compounded annually. Find the compound interest after 2 years.

For **2 years**, the effective **Compound Interest** rate = R + R + (R×R)/100.

Effective Rate = 2 + 2 + (2×2)/100 = **4.04%**.

Compound Interest = 4.04% of ₹25,000.

CI = 25,000 × (4.04/100) = 250 × 4.04 = ₹1,010.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,010.**

⇒ A = 25,000 × 1.0404

⇒ A = 26,010

⇒ CI = 26,010 − 25,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,010.**

questions.question: A keg is fitted with three taps A, B and C. If opened together, all the three taps will drain the full keg in 1(1)/(2) minutes. Taps A and B together take 3 minutes to drain the keg while taps B and C together take 4(1)/(2) minutes to drain it. How long (in minutes) taps A and C together take to drain the keg?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Work** as the LCM of 1.5, 3, and 4.5 = 9 units.

**Efficiency** of (A+B+C) = 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6 units/min.

**Efficiency** of (A+B) = 3 units/min and (B+C) = 2 units/min.

Efficiency of **Tap A** = 6 − 2 = 4; Efficiency of **Tap C** = 6 − 3 = 3.

Efficiency of (**A+C**) = 4 + 3 = 7 units/min.

**∴ The correct answer is 9/7 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B + C) = 1.5 min

Time taken by (A + B) = 3 min

Time taken by (B + C) = 4.5 min

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **Tap C** = Efficiency(A+B+C) − Efficiency(A+B)

⇒ Efficiency of **Tap C** = 6 − 3 = 3 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of **Tap A** = Efficiency(A+B+C) − Efficiency(B+C)

⇒ Efficiency of **Tap A** = 6 − 2 = 4 units/min

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (**A + C**) = 4 + 3 = 7 units/min

⇒ Time taken by (A + C) = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken by (A + C) = 9 ÷ 7 = 9/7 min

**∴ The correct answer is 9/7 min.**

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete the work (E = W/T).

Combined Work

When multiple pipes or taps work together, their **individual efficiencies** are added to find the net draining or filling rate.

LCM Method

Using the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given times as the total work simplifies complex fraction calculations into simple integer arithmetic.

questions.question: A park is designed in the shape of a right-angled triangle, where the two shorter sides measure 13 m and 84 m. A circular track with a uniform width of 2 m is constructed such that its outer boundary coincides with the circumcircle of the triangular park. Determine the perimeter of the inner boundary of this circular track.
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ In a **right-angled triangle**, the **hypotenuse** acts as the diameter of the **circumcircle**. Hypotenuse = √(13² + 84²) = √(169 + 7056) = 85 m. Outer radius (R) = 85 ÷ 2 = 42.5 m. Inner radius (r) = 42.5 − 2 = 40.5 m (subtracting the 2 m track width). Perimeter of the inner boundary = 2 × π × 40.5 = 81π m. **∴ The correct answer is 81π m.**

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tree from a point on the ground is 30°. After moving 10 m towards the tree, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. Find the height of the tree.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **angles of elevation** θ₁ and θ₂ from two points at a distance **d** apart on the same side of a **tree** of height **h**:

**h = d / (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)**

Here, d = 10 m, θ₁ = 30°, and θ₂ = 60°.

⇒ h = 10 / (cot 30° − cot 60°) = 10 / (√3 − 1/√3)

⇒ h = 10 / ((3 − 1) / √3) = (10 × √3) / 2 = 5√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Angle of elevation at point **A** = 30°, angle at point **B** = 60°, and distance **AB** = 10 m.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = **Perpendicular** / **Base**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2c02f28063e231d7d7d44208e47a58b10bed65661e3916b574722d2de286d90.png] 

⇒ Let the **height** of the tree **CD** be **h** and distance **BC** be **x**.

⇒ In right Δ**BCD**: tan 60° = h / x

⇒ √3 = h / x ⇒ x = h / √3

⇒ In right Δ**ACD**: tan 30° = h / (AB + BC)

⇒ 1 / √3 = h / (10 + x)

⇒ 1 / √3 = h / (10 + h / √3)

⇒ 10 + h / √3 = h√3

⇒ 10 = h√3 − h / √3

⇒ 10 = (3h − h) / √3

⇒ 10 = 2h / √3

⇒ 2h = 10√3 ⇒ h = 5√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an observer looks at an object above the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios for 30° and 60°

tan 30° = 1/√3 and tan 60° = √3. Note that as the observer moves **towards** the object, the **angle of elevation** increases.

General Formula for Distance

The distance **d** between two points of observation is given by d = h(cot θ₁ − cot θ₂), where h is the height.

questions.question: The 5-digit number 7a35b is divisible by 45, where a and b are positive integers. What is the value of (a + b)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be divisible by **45**, it must be divisible by both **5** and **9**.

Divisibility by **5**: The last digit **b** must be 0 or 5. Since **b** is a **positive integer**, **b = 5**.

Divisibility by **9**: The sum of digits (7 + a + 3 + 5 + 5) = 20 + a must be a multiple of 9.

The nearest multiple of 9 greater than 20 is 27. Therefore, 20 + a = 27 ⇒ **a = 7**.

The value of (a + b) = 7 + 5 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

questions.question: Yogesh invested a certain sum of money at 10% per annum. After 2 years, he received ₹147 as compound interest, compounded annually. Find the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) for 2 years at the same rate.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of **Compound Interest (CI)** for 2 years at 10% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10 / 100) = 21%.

Effective rate of **Simple Interest (SI)** for 2 years at 10% = 10 × 2 = 20%.

According to the question: 21% = ₹147.

So, 1% = 147 ÷ 21 = ₹7.

Therefore, 20% (SI) = 20 × 7 = ₹140.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Compound Interest (CI)** = ₹147

**Rate (R)** = 10% per annum

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa7b1724c46345001cff59b4acaaf7cd72690cc4419541cd70bc2d041d0daab6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 147 = P[(1 + 10/100)² − 1]

⇒ 147 = P[(11/10)² − 1]

⇒ 147 = P[121/100 − 1]

⇒ 147 = P[21/100]

⇒ P = (147 × 100) ÷ 21 = 7 × 100 = ₹700

⇒ Now, SI for 2 years = (700 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 7 × 10 × 2 = ₹140

**∴ The correct answer is ₹140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct SI-CI Relation for 2 Years

For a period of 2 years, the relationship is given by: SI = CI × 200 ÷ (200 + R). In this case, 147 × 200 ÷ 210 = ₹140.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference (D) for 2 years is calculated as: D = CI − SI = P(R/100)². Here, D = 147 − 140 = ₹7.

Successive Rate Formula

Compound interest for 2 years can be treated as a successive percentage change: Effective Rate = x + y + (xy/100).

questions.question: Ram has ₹1000 in the denomination of ₹10, ₹20 and ₹5 notes. If the number of ₹10 notes is 16 more than that of ₹20 notes and the number of ₹5 notes is twice the number of ₹20 notes, find the total number of notes that Ram has.
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Let the number of **₹20 notes** be x. questions.question: Two trains, A and B, start simultaneously from stations Delhi and Mumbai respectively towards each other on parallel tracks. After meeting, train A takes 16 hours to reach Mumbai, and train B takes 9 hours to reach Delhi. If train A’s speed is 60 km/h, what is the length of train B (in meters), given that it crosses a pole in 18 seconds?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds after meeting: SA / SB = √(TimeB / TimeA)

60 / SB = √(9 / 16) = 3 / 4

SB = (60 × 4) / 3 = 80 km/h

Speed of Train B in m/s = 80 × (5 / 18) = 400 / 18 m/s

Length of Train B = Speed × Crossing Time = (400 / 18) × 18 = 400 m

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **Train A** (SA) = 60 km/h

Time taken by **Train A** to reach Mumbai after meeting (tA) = 16 hr

Time taken by **Train B** to reach Delhi after meeting (tB) = 9 hr

Time taken by **Train B** to cross a pole = 18 sec

**Formula Used:**

1. SA / SB = √(tB / tA)

2. Distance = Speed × Time

3. km/h to m/s conversion: Speed × (5 / 18)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04bb618ee46c5a1f3b9c9b8db4735a1fb7aa45a0ea8ac3fdaf51a6a61745fc47.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 60 / SB = √(9 / 16)

⇒ 60 / SB = 3 / 4

⇒ 3 × SB = 60 × 4

⇒ SB = 240 / 3 = 80 km/h

⇒ Speed of Train B in m/s = 80 × (5 / 18) = 400 / 18 m/s

⇒ Length of Train B = Speed × Time to cross pole

⇒ Length of Train B = (400 / 18) × 18

⇒ Length of Train B = 400 m

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Time Formula

If two objects start at the same time and meet at a point, the time they take to meet is T = √(t₁ × t₂), where t₁ and t₂ are times taken to reach destinations after meeting.

Train Crossing a Pole

When a train crosses a stationary object of negligible length (pole, man, tree), the distance traveled is equal to the **length of the train** itself.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: Two solid hemispheres are joined together to make a sphere. The total surface area of solids reduced by approximately ___%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total surface area (TSA) of **one solid hemisphere** = 3 units (πr² factor).

TSA of **two separate hemispheres** = 3 + 3 = 6 units.

Surface area of the **resulting sphere** = 4 units.

Reduction = 6 − 4 = 2 units.

Percentage Reduction = (2 ÷ 6) × 100 = 33.33%.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two identical **solid hemispheres** are joined at their flat bases to form a **sphere** of the same radius **r**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Surface Area of a **Solid Hemisphere** = 3πr²

⇒ Surface Area of a **Sphere** = 4πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e7f0fd52f2e2a3c8e322e85ef8932175be4e528b9c69aba386999d3223aab9b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined TSA of two separate hemispheres = 2 × 3πr² = 6πr²

⇒ Surface Area of the single sphere formed = 4πr²

⇒ Reduction in Surface Area = 6πr² − 4πr² = 2πr²

⇒ Percentage Reduction = (Reduction ÷ Original Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage Reduction = (2πr² ÷ 6πr²) × 100

⇒ Percentage Reduction = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 ≈ 33.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Hemisphere

The area of only the curved part of a hemisphere is 2πr². The **flat base** has an area of πr².

Volume Conservation

When solids are joined or melted, the **total volume** remains constant. Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³.

Total Surface Area of Solid Hemisphere

TSA = CSA + Base Area = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr².

questions.question: Lekhraj sells an article at a profit of 25%. If the cost price is increased by 20% and the selling price is reduced by 10%, what percentage loss will Lekhraj incur?

**Net Loss** = 120 − 112.5 = 7.5.

questions.question: In a science experiment, chemicals X, Y, and Z are mixed in the ratio 5:2:3. If the total weight of the mixture is 100 grams, how much of chemical Y is present?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **ratio parts** = 5 + 2 + 3 = 10 units.

10 units = **100 g** (Total weight).

1 unit = 10 g.

**Chemical Y** share = 2 units = 2 × 10 = 20 g.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of **Chemical X** : **Chemical Y** : **Chemical Z** = 5 : 2 : 3

Total **weight** of the **mixture** = **100 g**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d5863aabb9667c04e733158a60bb5ecb04b85eb0821df562716ebfb9a786955.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the weight of **Chemical X** be 5k, **Chemical Y** be 2k, and **Chemical Z** be 3k.

⇒ Total weight = 5k + 2k + 3k = 10k

⇒ 10k = 100

⇒ k = 100 ÷ 10

⇒ k = 10 g

⇒ Weight of **Chemical Y** = 2k = 2 × 10

⇒ Weight of **Chemical Y** = 20 g

**∴ The correct answer is 20 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportions

A **ratio** indicates how many times one number contains another. To divide a quantity in a given ratio, the total quantity is divided by the sum of the ratio terms to find the value of one **unit**.

Percentage in Mixtures

The **percentage** of any component can be found by (Component Ratio / Total Ratio) × 100. In this case, **Chemical Y** is (2/10) × 100 = 20% of the total **mixture**.

questions.question: Find the measure of the unknown interior angle in an irregular hexagon with angles 140°, 80°, 145°, 155°, and 100°.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of **interior angles** of a **hexagon** (n = 6) = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°.

Sum of 5 given angles = 140° + 80° + 145° + 155° + 100° = 620°.

Unknown angle = 720° − 620° = 100°.

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Angles of an **irregular hexagon** are 140°, 80°, 145°, 155°, and 100°.

**Formula Used:** Sum of interior angles of a polygon = (n − 2) × 180°, where n is the number of sides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d403b9cf84757d5146050fa569e428b585439167f966f1a6dbbe0bb456209b0f.png] 

For a **hexagon**, n = 6:

⇒ Sum = (6 − 2) × 180°

⇒ Sum = 4 × 180°

⇒ Sum = 720°

Let the unknown 6th angle be **x**.

⇒ 140° + 80° + 145° + 155° + 100° + x = 720°

⇒ 620° + x = 720°

⇒ x = 720° − 620°

⇒ x = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Polygon Interior Angles Theorem

The sum of the interior angles of any convex polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°, where n represents the number of sides.

Exterior Angle Sum

For any convex polygon, the sum of the exterior angles (one at each vertex) is always equal to 360° regardless of the number of sides.

Regular Hexagon

In a **regular hexagon**, all interior angles are equal, and each angle measures 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.
